def sharedInstance (P : Parameters) : Instance where
  toolCount := P.tools
  compatibility := List.replicate P.certificate.stages Finset.univ

theorem stageCount_eq (P : Parameters) : P.sharedInstance.stageCount = P.certificate.stages := by
  simp [sharedInstance, Instance.stageCount]

theorem eligible_eq_univ (P : Parameters) (i : P.sharedInstance.Stage) :
    P.sharedInstance.eligible i = Finset.univ := by
  have h : P.sharedInstance.eligible i ∈ P.sharedInstance.compatibility := List.get_mem _ i
  change P.sharedInstance.eligible i ∈ List.replicate P.certificate.stages Finset.univ at h
  exact List.eq_of_mem_replicate h

def experiment (P : Parameters) : Statistics.BinaryExperiment where
  alphabetSize := 2
  priorOne := 1 / 2
  prior_pos := by norm_num
  prior_lt_one := by norm_num
  channel x y :=
    if y.val = (if x then 1 else 0) then 1 / 2 + P.certificate.gamma
    else 1 / 2 - P.certificate.gamma
  channel_pos := by
    intro x y
    split_ifs <;> linarith [P.certificate.gamma_pos, P.certificate.gamma_le_quarter]
  channel_sum := by
    intro x
    cases x <;> norm_num [Fin.sum_univ_two]
  channel_distinct := by
    intro heq
    have h := congrFun heq (0 : Fin 2)
    norm_num at h
    linarith [P.certificate.gamma_pos]
  observationFee := P.reviewFee
  observationFee_pos := P.reviewFee_pos

def input (P : Parameters) (fee : ℚ) (hfee : 0 ≤ fee) : StatisticalInput P.sharedInstance where
  experiment := fun _ => P.experiment
  correctionFee := fun _ _ => fee
  correctionFee_nonneg := fun _ _ => hfee

theorem input_same_experiment (P : Parameters) (fee fee' : ℚ)
    (hfee : 0 ≤ fee) (hfee' : 0 ≤ fee') :
    (P.input fee hfee).experiment = (P.input fee' hfee').experiment := rfl

theorem actual_correctionFee (P : Parameters) (fee : ℚ) (hfee : 0 ≤ fee)
    (i : P.sharedInstance.Stage) (r : P.sharedInstance.Tool) :
    (P.input fee hfee).fees.correction i r = fee := rfl

abbrev PaymentContract (P : Parameters) := {C : Contract P.sharedInstance // C.IsCurrentPayment}

def paymentContract (P : Parameters) (quota : P.sharedInstance.Stage → ℕ) (H H0 : ℕ) :
    P.PaymentContract :=
  ⟨⟨.early, .currentWindow, .currentWindow, quota, H, H0⟩, ⟨⟨rfl, rfl⟩, rfl⟩⟩

/-- Exactly the existing real-policy constrained infimum, with the same
current-payment contract and actual-execution billing. Normal C0 fees remain
the independent NormalCharges interface, as in the frozen variable bill. -/
noncomputable def paidValue (P : Parameters) (C : P.PaymentContract)
    (mode : Native.ResourceMode) (accounting : Native.NormalAccounting P.sharedInstance)
    (fee : ℚ) (hfee : 0 ≤ fee) : ℝ≥0∞ :=

original_evidence.text:
The structural law above fixes correction fees while confidence increases.
This section isolates the effect of a fee that may vary with the other
parameters.  It is a restricted extension: all $K<N$ tools can correct
every output, facts are independent fair bits, and every review is a
homogeneous BSC of accuracy $1/2+\gamma$ costing $c$.
Assume rational $c>0$, $0<\gamma\le1/4$, $f\ge0$ and
$0<\delta\le1/64$.  Each actual correction costs the same $f$.
The hypotheses concerning freshness, genuine mismatch handles, exact
early reports, guaranteed one-use corrections and all-path charging
remain as in Section~\ref{sec:model}.

We strengthen the current-allocation contract to \emph{current payment},
denoted $I_{\rm pay}$: a wrong output must be physically corrected and
paid for before advance.  An irrevocable allocation with execution or
payment withheld until a later decision is not this contract.
All lawful randomized visible-history policies remain in the comparison,
including non-MAP writes, abandonment and spending on eventual failures.
Original review quotas and the total call cap remain in force; there is
no additional hard monetary spending cap.

Let $R_{\rm act}$ count physically executed corrections.  Define
$V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)$ as the infimum of
\begin{equation}
 \E C=\E\!\left[c\sum_{i=1}^N T_i+fR_{\rm act}\right]
 \quad\text{subject to }\Prob(\mathrm{failure})\le\delta
 \label{eq:paid:bill}
\end{equation}
in this original instance.  Let $V_f^\infty(\delta)$ relax only review
and call caps, retaining the same correction rights and payment contract.
Write $h=\log((1+2\gamma)/(1-2\gamma))$ and $a=c/(2\gamma h)$ as before.
Appendix~\ref{app:paid:proofs} gives an explicit integer
$Q=Q(N,\gamma,\delta)$, independent of $f$, in
\eqref{eq:paid:certificate-numbers}.  The sufficient native qualification is
\begin{equation}
 \text{each original stage admits $Q$ reviews and its lawful operations},
 \qquad H\ge H_0+NQ+K.
 \label{eq:paid:cap-certificate}
\end{equation}
It is a test of the original resources, not permission to enlarge them.
It is separate from the fixed-structure certificate
in Appendix~\ref{subsec:price-native}.

original_evidence.text:
The structural law above fixes correction fees while confidence increases.
This section isolates the effect of a fee that may vary with the other
parameters.  It is a restricted extension: all $K<N$ tools can correct
every output, facts are independent fair bits, and every review is a
homogeneous BSC of accuracy $1/2+\gamma$ costing $c$.
Assume rational $c>0$, $0<\gamma\le1/4$, $f\ge0$ and
$0<\delta\le1/64$.  Each actual correction costs the same $f$.
The hypotheses concerning freshness, genuine mismatch handles, exact
early reports, guaranteed one-use corrections and all-path charging
remain as in Section~\ref{sec:model}.

We strengthen the current-allocation contract to \emph{current payment},
denoted $I_{\rm pay}$: a wrong output must be physically corrected and
paid for before advance.  An irrevocable allocation with execution or
payment withheld until a later decision is not this contract.
All lawful randomized visible-history policies remain in the comparison,
including non-MAP writes, abandonment and spending on eventual failures.
Original review quotas and the total call cap remain in force; there is
no additional hard monetary spending cap.

Let $R_{\rm act}$ count physically executed corrections.  Define
$V_f^{\rm nat}(\delta)$ as the infimum of
\begin{equation}
 \E C=\E\!\left[c\sum_{i=1}^N T_i+fR_{\rm act}\right]
 \quad\text{subject to }\Prob(\mathrm{failure})\le\delta
 \label{eq:paid:bill}
\end{equation}
in this original instance.  Let $V_f^\infty(\delta)$ relax only review
and call caps, retaining the same correction rights and payment contract.
Write $h=\log((1+2\gamma)/(1-2\gamma))$ and $a=c/(2\gamma h)$ as before.
Appendix~\ref{app:paid:proofs} gives an explicit integer
$Q=Q(N,\gamma,\delta)$, independent of $f$, in
\eqref{eq:paid:certificate-numbers}.  The sufficient native qualification is
\begin{equation}
 \text{each original stage admits $Q$ reviews and its lawful operations},
 \qquad H\ge H_0+NQ+K.
 \label{eq:paid:cap-certificate}
\end{equation}
It is a test of the original resources, not permission to enlarge them.
It is separate from the fixed-structure certificate
in Appendix~\ref{subsec:price-native}.

Set
\[
 \phi(p)=(1-2p)\log\frac{1-p}{p},\qquad 0<p\le1/2.
\]
It is decreasing and convex, with
$\phi''(p)=1/[p^2(1-p)^2]$.  For a stopped fair-BSC experiment let $P$
be its posterior MAP error, before any truth report.

\begin{lemma}[Stopped information]
\label{lem:paid:information}
For every experiment with finite expected review count,
\begin{equation}
 c\E T=a\E\phi(P).
 \label{eq:paid:information}
\end{equation}
The identity also holds after restriction to an event determined before
the current fresh fact is born.  A fact filled blindly for analysis has
$T=0$ and $P=1/2$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Orient each log-likelihood increment by the true bit.  Its conditional
mean before purchase is $\kappa$ and its absolute value is $h$.
Summing predictable increments gives expected stopped score
$\kappa\E T$; finite expected $T$ justifies the interchange since the
increments are bounded.  Conditional on the stopped transcript, if the
posterior of bit one is $\theta$, the expected oriented score is
$(2\theta-1)\log(\theta/(1-\theta))=\phi(P)$.
This proves the identity.  Conditional on generated pre-birth history,
freshness preserves the fair prior and original channel.  Apply the same
argument there and average the indicated pre-birth event.  No step
conditions on eventual success.
\end{proof}

For $m\ge0$, define
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf C_m=\frac{cm}{2\gamma}(1-2p_m)
     =a\,mh\tanh(mh/2),\qquad (p_0,\mathsf C_0)=(1/2,0).
 \label{eq:paid:roc-points}
\end{equation}
The notation $\mathsf C_m$ denotes local review charges, distinct from the normal full-run charge $C_0$.
Let $g(p)$ be the piecewise-linear interpolation of the adjacent points
$(p_m,\mathsf C_m)$, and set $g(0)=+\infty$.

\begin{lemma}[Exact randomized local ROC]
\label{lem:paid:roc}
The minimum expected review charge of a MAP experiment with average error
exactly $p\in(0,1/2]$ is $g(p)$.  The minimum for an arbitrary binary
decision of error $e\in(0,1)$ is
$\widetilde g(e)=g(\min\{e,1-e\})$.
Each $g(p)$ is attained by randomizing two adjacent symmetric likelihood
boundary tests.  For rational $p,c,\gamma$, their probabilities and mean
charges are rational and explicitly computable.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
After any stopped record, including its private seed, posterior odds are
$R^s$ for an integer signed observation sum $s$.  Thus $P=p_m$ for some
$m=|s|$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:information}, the error/cost pair is a convex
combination of $(p_m,a\phi(p_m))=(p_m,\mathsf C_m)$.
Strict convexity of $\phi$ makes their adjacent chords the lower convex
boundary.  Consequently a MAP experiment of mean error $p$ costs at
least $g(p)$.

The symmetric random walk stopped at $\pm m$ has posterior error exactly
$p_m$.  Its finite absorbing walk has finite mean duration, and stopped
drift gives
\[
 \E T_m=\frac{m}{2\gamma}(1-2p_m).
\]

For $m\ge0$, define
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf C_m=\frac{cm}{2\gamma}(1-2p_m)
     =a\,mh\tanh(mh/2),\qquad (p_0,\mathsf C_0)=(1/2,0).
 \label{eq:paid:roc-points}
\end{equation}
The notation $\mathsf C_m$ denotes local review charges, distinct from the normal full-run charge $C_0$.
Let $g(p)$ be the piecewise-linear interpolation of the adjacent points
$(p_m,\mathsf C_m)$, and set $g(0)=+\infty$.

\begin{lemma}[Exact randomized local ROC]
\label{lem:paid:roc}
The minimum expected review charge of a MAP experiment with average error
exactly $p\in(0,1/2]$ is $g(p)$.  The minimum for an arbitrary binary
decision of error $e\in(0,1)$ is
$\widetilde g(e)=g(\min\{e,1-e\})$.
Each $g(p)$ is attained by randomizing two adjacent symmetric likelihood
boundary tests.  For rational $p,c,\gamma$, their probabilities and mean
charges are rational and explicitly computable.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
After any stopped record, including its private seed, posterior odds are
$R^s$ for an integer signed observation sum $s$.  Thus $P=p_m$ for some
$m=|s|$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:information}, the error/cost pair is a convex
combination of $(p_m,a\phi(p_m))=(p_m,\mathsf C_m)$.
Strict convexity of $\phi$ makes their adjacent chords the lower convex
boundary.  Consequently a MAP experiment of mean error $p$ costs at
least $g(p)$.

The symmetric random walk stopped at $\pm m$ has posterior error exactly
$p_m$.  Its finite absorbing walk has finite mean duration, and stopped
drift gives
\[
 \E T_m=\frac{m}{2\gamma}(1-2p_m).
\]
It therefore attains $\mathsf C_m$.  Mixing adjacent boundaries attains each
chord.  For any decision and its complement, both conditional error
probabilities are at least the posterior MAP error.  Hence
$\min(e,1-e)\ge\E P$.  Convexity and monotonicity yield
$\E C\ge g(\E P)\ge\widetilde g(e)$.  Complementing the symmetric
decision when $e>1/2$ attains this bound.  Finally $R^m,p_m,\mathsf C_m$ and
adjacent interpolation weights are rational for rational inputs.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Record-level representation]
\label{lem:paid:representation}
In the cap-relaxed model, every finite-cost full-history policy is first
dominated by the policy that stops at permanent failure.  This dominated
policy can be simulated by symmetric integer boundary experiments and
private auxiliary records, preserving its virtual write-error,
correction, and abandonment history law up to termination, with no greater
expected review charge.  Conditional on an auxiliary writing record of
posterior level $m$, its mean review charge is $\mathsf C_m$, and its decision
error is either $p_m$ or $1-p_m$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Let $\pi_{\rm stop}$ be the input policy stopped at permanent failure.
It has the same success event and no greater cost than the input policy.
Condition on a generated virtual history before a fresh stage.  Let $Z$ be
the local record of $\pi_{\rm stop}$, containing its seed, observations, and
binary decision or abandonment label, but not a later truth report.
For analysis fill an unmade decision on abandonment; an unopened fact
has level zero.  Given a record $z$, let $m(z)$ be the magnitude of its
integer likelihood score and $s(z)$ its MAP orientation, with a fixed
tie convention.  The conditional truth distribution depends only on
this signed score: for a fixed record, the policy's sampling and
stopping factors do not depend on the hidden bit.

Sample $z$ from its original marginal law before observing the actual
fresh bit.  Run the symmetric level-$m(z)$ test and let $s'$ be its MAP
orientation.  Define the private coordinate flip $b=s(z)\mathbin\oplus s'$.
If $z$ writes $d(z)$, actually write $d(z)\mathbin\oplus b$.
After the actual report, the virtual truth $X\mathbin\oplus b$ differs
from $s(z)$ with probability exactly $p_{m(z)}$, conditional on $z$.
It therefore has the original posterior law.  The actual and virtual
write-error indicators agree.  Feed $z$ and this virtual report to the
old controller; genuine physical correction uses the actual mismatch
handle.  Future facts remain independent of this private virtual history.
Repeating the construction preserves the marked history law.

mean review charge satisfies

\]

nonnegative testing charge; this gives the stated no-greater bound.

aggregated-error projection supplies only the inequality in

kernels; finite-cost truncation gives the same assertion at infima.

theorem uniformLocalSurrogate (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) : P.UniformLocalSurrogate := by
  constructor
  · intro p hp hhalf
    have hb := rocChord_surrogate_bounds P.binarySymmetric p hp hhalf
    have he : P.rocSurrogate p = ENNReal.ofReal
        (max (P.binarySymmetric.a * phiReal p)
          ((P.binarySymmetric.reviewFee : ℝ) / (P.binarySymmetric.gamma : ℝ) * (1 / 2 - p))) := by
      rw [PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters.rocSurrogate, phi_of_pos hp,
        ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul P.a_pos.le,
        ← ENNReal.ofReal_mul (show 0 ≤ (P.reviewFee : ℝ) / (P.certificate.gamma : ℝ) by
          exact div_nonneg (by exact_mod_cast P.reviewFee_pos.le)
            (by exact_mod_cast P.certificate.gamma_pos.le)), ENNReal.ofReal_max]
      rfl
    rw [he, P.binarySymmetric.rocPrice_of_pos p hp hhalf]
    constructor
    · exact ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal hb.1
    · have h := ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal hb.2
      simpa only [ENNReal.ofReal_mul (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 4), ENNReal.ofReal_ofNat] using h
  · exact endpointCharge_succ_le_four P.binarySymmetric

original_evidence.text:
This is a comparison proof, not an efficient compiler for an unknown
policy.  The algorithm below needs no trace-distribution oracle.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A uniformly attainable local bound]
\label{lem:paid:surrogate}
For $0<p\le1/2$, put
\[
 \psi(p)=\max\{a\phi(p),(c/\gamma)(1/2-p)\}.
\]
Then $\psi(p)\le g(p)\le4\psi(p)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
On $[p_1,1/2]$, where $p_1=1/2-\gamma$, the first ROC chord is
$(c/\gamma)(1/2-p)$ and dominates $a\phi(p)$ by convexity.
For $p\le p_1$, writing $u=1/2-p$ gives
$a\phi(p)=(c/\gamma)u\log((1-p)/p)/h\ge(c/\gamma)u$.
If $p_{m+1}\le p\le p_m$ with $m\ge1$, concavity of $\tanh$ gives
\[
 \frac{\mathsf C_{m+1}}{\mathsf C_m}
 \le\left(\frac{m+1}{m}\right)^2\le4.
\]

For analysis stop at the first permanent failure or original abandonment,
retaining every earlier charge.  An erroneous output not corrected before
its current window closes is permanent failure.  Fill only a current
unmade decision by MAP.  An abandonment between stages is assigned to the
next required stage, if one remains, using a fresh analysis-only fair bit
with zero observations.  Do not fill all future stages.  No original
successful path is removed.

Let $A_i$ be eligibility for this truncated stage experiment, determined
before bit $i$ is born, and let $\mu_i=\Prob(A_i)$.  Every original
successful path enters every stage, so $\mu_i\ge1-\delta$.

or filled wrong decision in the truncated execution either receives an
actual correction or is assigned to the first failure/abandonment at
that stage.  These assigned failure events are disjoint.  Consequently
\begin{equation}
 b:=\sum_i\E[\ind_{A_i}P_i]\le r+\delta.
 \label{eq:paid:one-failure-allowance}
\end{equation}
The allowance is $\delta$, rather than $N\delta$, because only the current
abandoned decision was filled.  Corrections already executed on a later
failing path remain in $r$.

Let $M'=\sum_i\mu_i\ge m$.  Weighted Jensen in
\eqref{eq:paid:surviving-information} gives observation charge at least
$aM'\phi(b/M')$.  Its argument is at most $1/2$.
Monotonicity of $\mathcal H$ and
\eqref{eq:paid:one-failure-allowance} give
$a\mathcal H(M',b)\ge a\mathcal H(m,r+\delta)$.
Add the actual bill $fr$.  If the original policy spends after permanent
failure, the analysis removed only nonnegative observations and may keep
the larger original $r$; the bound remains valid.  Native finite quotas
justify stopped summation directly.  In the relaxed model finite expected
cost gives integrability; infinite-cost policies need no bound.

\label{lem:paid:usage}
For every native $\delta$-safe policy, if $r=\E R_{\rm act}$ and
$m=N(1-\delta)$, then
\begin{equation}
 \E C\ge a\mathcal H(m,r+\delta)+fr.
 \label{eq:paid:usage}

The same inequality holds for finite-cost cap-relaxed policies.

For analysis stop at the first permanent failure or original abandonment,
retaining every earlier charge.  An erroneous output not corrected before
its current window closes is permanent failure.  Fill only a current
unmade decision by MAP.  An abandonment between stages is assigned to the
next required stage, if one remains, using a fresh analysis-only fair bit
with zero observations.  Do not fill all future stages.  No original
successful path is removed.

its success event and does not increase its charge.  Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:representation} to this dominated policy.  Conditional on
an auxiliary writing record $z$, let $p=p_{m(z)}$ be its MAP error and
$d(z)$ its virtual output.  Its conditional decision error is $e=p$ if
that decision is MAP and $e=1-p$ otherwise.  In both cases $e\ge p$.
Copy a virtual abandonment, deleting nonnegative work.

For a writing record, run an actual MAP experiment of exact error
$p'=\min\{p,p_f\}$.  After its real report let $E'$ be the actual error.
If $E'=1$, declare the virtual error $E=1$.  If $E'=0$, declare $E=1$
with probability
\begin{equation}
 \frac{e-p'}{1-p'}.
 \label{eq:paid:false-positive-virtual-error}
\end{equation}
This is a valid probability.  It gives $\Prob(E=1\mid z)=e$ and
$E'\le E$ pathwise.  Feed the virtual truth $d(z)\mathbin\oplus E$ to
the old controller.  Conditional on $z$ this truth has exactly its
original posterior law, even for a non-MAP output.  Therefore the virtual
controller reproduces the dominated stopped free policy's marked history
up to termination.  That policy has no greater charge and the same
success event as the input free policy.

each next fact; no future truth is inspected.

correction or abandons, the simulator may abandon as well.  Every virtual
successful path is an actual successful path, proving the risk claim.

/-- A_(n,k), defined at a nonterminal n by the genuine fresh successor F. -/
noncomputable def paidGoodSuccessor (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters)
    (fee : ℚ) (hfee : 0 ≤ fee) (n k : ℕ) (penalty : ℝ≥0∞) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  P.freshPaidPenalty fee hfee (n - 1) k penalty

/-- B_(n,k): a real correction is paid immediately, or the task abandons.
No allocation-only or delayed-payment alternative is introduced. -/
noncomputable def paidBadSuccessor (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters)
    (fee : ℚ) (hfee : 0 ≤ fee) (n k : ℕ) (penalty : ℝ≥0∞) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  match k with
  | 0 => penalty
  | next + 1 => min penalty (ENNReal.ofReal (fee : ℝ) + P.freshPaidPenalty fee hfee (n - 1) next penalty)

noncomputable def paidEndpointObjective (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters)
    (fee : ℚ) (hfee : 0 ≤ fee) (n k : ℕ) (penalty : ℝ≥0∞) (m : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ENNReal.ofReal (P.binarySymmetric.endpointCharge m : ℝ) +
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 - (P.binarySymmetric.endpointError m : ℝ)) * P.paidGoodSuccessor fee hfee n k penalty +
    ENNReal.ofReal (P.binarySymmetric.endpointError m : ℝ) * P.paidBadSuccessor fee hfee n k penalty

def IsPaidEndpointMinimizer (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters)
    (fee : ℚ) (hfee : 0 ≤ fee) (n k : ℕ) (penalty : ℝ≥0∞) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ index : ℕ, P.paidEndpointObjective fee hfee n k penalty m ≤
    P.paidEndpointObjective fee hfee n k penalty index

def IsLeastPaidEndpointMinimizer (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters)
    (fee : ℚ) (hfee : 0 ≤ fee) (n k : ℕ) (penalty : ℝ≥0∞) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  P.IsPaidEndpointMinimizer fee hfee n k penalty m ∧
    ∀ other : ℕ, P.IsPaidEndpointMinimizer fee hfee n k penalty other → m ≤ other

def PaidSuccessorOrder (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) : Prop :=

and, if needed, a version-bound mismatch handle. A correction requires

early-report workflows the report arrives before the next fact is
born. A late-report workflow receives all reports after all ordinary
writes; advance depends on the write, so delay causes no deadlock.

structure MenuEntry where
  action : MenuAction
  observation : ℚ
  repairs : ℚ
  failure : ℚ
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

def MenuEntry.objective (entry : MenuEntry) (fee penalty : ℚ) : ℚ :=
  entry.observation + fee * entry.repairs + penalty * entry.failure

def finishEntry : MenuEntry := ⟨.finish, 0, 0, 0⟩
def abandonEntry : MenuEntry := ⟨.abandon, 0, 0, 1⟩

/-- A paid bad branch adds one REAL execution to the stored mean. The
controller will allocate and execute it using its genuine mismatch handle. -/
def repairEntry (child : MenuEntry) : MenuEntry :=
  { child with repairs := 1 + child.repairs }

abbrev MenuRow := Array MenuEntry
abbrev MenuTable := Array MenuRow

def baseMenuRow (tools : ℕ) : MenuRow := Array.replicate (tools + 1) finishEntry

/-- One original independent fair-guess bit for each physical stage. The
finite product is fixed before the run and is independent of its World. -/
abbrev MenuSeed (N K : ℕ) := (freshInstance N K).Stage → Bool

noncomputable def menuSeedLaw (N K : ℕ) : Measure (MenuSeed N K) :=
  Measure.pi (fun _ : (freshInstance N K).Stage => Statistics.BinarySymmetric.Parameters.fairGuessLaw)

instance menuSeedLaw_probability (N K : ℕ) : IsProbabilityMeasure (menuSeedLaw N K) := by
  unfold menuSeedLaw
  infer_instance

theorem menuSeedLaw_eval (N K : ℕ) (stage : (freshInstance N K).Stage) :
    (menuSeedLaw N K).map (Function.eval stage) = Statistics.BinarySymmetric.Parameters.fairGuessLaw :=
  (measurePreserving_eval
    (fun _ : (freshInstance N K).Stage => Statistics.BinarySymmetric.Parameters.fairGuessLaw) stage).map_eq

theorem menuSeedLaw_independent (N K : ℕ) :

Each table entry stores its selected action, expected observation charge,
expected actual correction count, and failure probability.  Their
recursions use the same weights $1-p_m,p_m$; current review charge is
$\mathsf C_m$ and a chosen correction adds one actual call.  Correlation of a
test's duration with its error does not invalidate these mean recursions:
the future chosen policies ignore that duration and freshness fixes their
conditional values.

Each table entry stores its selected action, expected observation charge,
expected actual correction count, and failure probability.  Their
recursions use the same weights $1-p_m,p_m$; current review charge is
$\mathsf C_m$ and a chosen correction adds one actual call.  Correlation of a
test's duration with its error does not invalidate these mean recursions:
the future chosen policies ignore that duration and freshness fixes their
conditional values.

An ordinary write fixes a selected bit and closes that slot's ordinary
write and review ports. Its authoritative report reveals the true bit
and, if needed, a version-bound mismatch handle. A correction requires
this actual handle; a blind guaranteed overwrite is not native. In
early-report workflows the report arrives before the next fact is
born. A late-report workflow receives all reports after all ordinary
writes; advance depends on the write, so delay causes no deadlock.

The current-window contract $I$ requires an erroneous output's tool
allocation to be irrevocable before advancing. A contract may also
require actual execution before advance. Our upper controllers execute
immediately, and the lower comparison permits the larger class in
which an already committed correction may be executed later. No such
tool can be reassigned. The retained contract $R$ instead keeps all
correction handles until a common terminal barrier and permits tools

At multiplier zero choose immediate abandonment of risk one and cost zero.
Maintain two exactly optimal endpoint policies with
$\lambda_L<\lambda_U$, risks $r_L>\delta\ge r_U$, and mean actual
costs $C_L,C_U$.  Bisect the multiplier interval and update the endpoint
according to its computed risk.  An optimal policy of risk exactly
$\delta$ can be returned immediately: its cost is
$F_{N,K}(\lambda)-\lambda\delta\le V_f^\infty(\delta)$ by weak duality,
and feasibility gives the reverse inequality.  Otherwise mix the endpoint
policies at the beginning with weight
\begin{equation}
 w=\frac{\delta-r_U}{r_L-r_U}
 \label{eq:paid:initial-mixture}
\end{equation}
on the lower endpoint.  Its risk is exactly $\delta$ and its mean cost
is $U=wC_L+(1-w)C_U$.

Let $L=F_{N,K}(\lambda_U)-\lambda_U\delta$.
Endpoint optimality gives
\[
 -\lambda_U\le\frac{C_L-C_U}{r_L-r_U}\le-\lambda_L.
\]
Thus, directly rather than by subtracting unrelated multiplicative
approximations,
\begin{equation}
 0\le U-L\le(\lambda_U-\lambda_L)(\delta-r_U)
                \le(\lambda_U-\lambda_L)\delta.
 \label{eq:paid:mixture-gap}
\end{equation}
Weak duality alone gives $L\le V_f^\infty(\delta)\le U$.
Stop when the rightmost expression is at most $U/2$; then
\begin{equation}
 U\le2V_f^\infty(\delta).
 \label{eq:paid:two-factor-reference}

An ordinary write fixes a selected bit and closes that slot's ordinary
write and review ports. Its authoritative report reveals the true bit
and, if needed, a version-bound mismatch handle. A correction requires
this actual handle; a blind guaranteed overwrite is not native. In
early-report workflows the report arrives before the next fact is
born. A late-report workflow receives all reports after all ordinary
writes; advance depends on the write, so delay causes no deadlock.

The current-window contract $I$ requires an erroneous output's tool
allocation to be irrevocable before advancing. A contract may also
require actual execution before advance. Our upper controllers execute
immediately, and the lower comparison permits the larger class in
which an already committed correction may be executed later. No such
tool can be reassigned. The retained contract $R$ instead keeps all
correction handles until a common terminal barrier and permits tools
to be assigned there. Original per-stage review quotas and a cumulative
call cap $H$ apply. There are no additional order-sensitive locks,
changing prices, cross-output effects or ways to reopen a review port.

Success means that all $N$ required final outputs are truly correct.
Abandonment, incomplete execution and unrepaired errors are failures.
A policy may use all visible history and private randomness, write
non-MAP values, decline corrections, delay where legal, and continue
spending after failure. Only the global condition
$\Prob(\mathrm{failure})\le\delta$ is imposed. If actual correction
$i,r$ costs a fixed $f_{ir}\ge0$, the variable bill is
\[
 C=\sum_i c_iT_i+\sum_{\text{actual corrections }(i,r)}f_{ir}.
\]
All failed-path charges count. Write $f_{\max}=\max f_{ir}$, or zero
when there is no compatible pair. Every policy uses at most
$\min(N,q)$ genuine corrections. Normal full-run fees $C_0$ are
accounted for separately; every successful run pays at least $C_0$,
and each constructed run pays at most $C_0$ in normal charges. Let
$H_0$ bound its normal calls on a complete execution. Local planning
work is reported as computation, separately from native calls.

There is an explicit termination bound even near zero value.  The
minimum risk with zero variable charges is
\begin{equation}
 \zeta_f=\begin{cases}
 \Prob\{\operatorname{Bin}(N,1/2)>K\},&f=0,\\
 1-2^{-N},&f>0.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:paid:zero-charge-risk}
\end{equation}
Without reviews every next predictable guess has independent error
$1/2$.  If $f=0$, at most $K$ such errors are repairable; if $f>0$, a
zero-charge policy cannot execute a correction, so it must guess all bits
correctly.  Filling unvisited guesses after abandonment proves these
lower bounds, and the corresponding blind policies attain them.
If $\delta\ge\zeta_f$, return that zero-cost native policy.

Otherwise let $b_f=c$ for $f=0$ and $b_f=\min\{c,f\}$ for $f>0$, and put
$\ell=b_f(\zeta_f-\delta)>0$.
Every $\delta$-safe policy costs at least $\ell$.
Indeed keep its behavior until just before its first positive-charge
operation, then replace the remainder by a zero-charge continuation.
This causal policy has risk at least $\zeta_f$ and can change failure

def walkUpdate (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) (level : ℕ) (truth : Bool) (previous : Array ℚ) : Array ℚ :=
  (List.finRange (2 * level + 1)).foldl (fun next state =>
    (List.finRange 2).foldl (fun next letter =>
      let target := walkMove level state letter
      next.setIfInBounds target.val
        (next.getD target.val 0 + previous.getD state.val 0 * P.experiment.channel truth letter)) next)
    (Array.replicate (2 * level + 1) 0)

/-- The finite absorbing random-walk table stores its preceding row once.
It never consults the actual test error or a performance oracle. -/
def walkRow (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) (level : ℕ) (truth : Bool) : ℕ → Array ℚ
  | 0 => Array.ofFn (fun state : WalkCell level => if state.val = level then 1 else 0)
  | steps + 1 => P.walkUpdate level truth (P.walkRow level truth steps)

def walkDistribution (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) (level : ℕ) (truth : Bool) (steps : ℕ)
    (state : WalkCell level) : ℚ := (P.walkRow level truth steps).getD state.val 0

/-- MAP loss at Q after absorption, with an independent fair tie. -/
def cappedError (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) (m : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  ∑ state : WalkCell (m + 1), P.walkDistribution (m + 1) true P.certificate.Q state *
    if state.val < m + 1 then 1 else if state.val = m + 1 then 1 / 2 else 0

def calibrationWeight (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) (m : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  (1 / 2 - P.binarySymmetric.endpointError m) / (1 / 2 - P.cappedError m)

target proves that the original rational omega itself lies in [0,1]. -/
def clippedCalibrationWeight (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) (m : ℕ) : Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 :=

original_evidence.text:
\paragraph{Bounded tests with exactly the same errors}

An endpoint policy still has unbounded review durations.  We now replace
each endpoint experiment by a bounded one without increasing its risk.
For $m=0$ write blindly.  For $1\le m\le M$, run the symmetric
level-$(m+1)$ test for at most $Q$ reviews, then write MAP, randomizing a
tie.  Call its actual error $q_m$.

Conditional on either truth, the unrestricted true-direction score has
increments of mean $\kappa$ in an interval of length $2h$.
On nonexit at time $Q$ its score is below $(m+1)h$.
Since $Q\ge(M+1)/\gamma=2(M+1)h/\kappa$, Hoeffding gives
\begin{equation}
 \Prob(T_{m+1}>Q)\le e^{-\gamma^2Q/2}
       \le e^{-E}\le2^{-E}\le\gamma\varepsilon.
 \label{eq:paid:bounded-tail}
\end{equation}
The logistic formula and \eqref{eq:paid:menu-floor} give
\[
 p_{m+1}\le(1-2\gamma)p_m,
 \qquad q_m\le p_{m+1}+\gamma\varepsilon
                   \le p_m-\gamma\varepsilon<p_m.
\]
Compute $q_m$ exactly with a length-$Q$ rational random-walk table,
absorbing at $\pm(m+1)$ and applying its terminal MAP/tie decision.

def calibratedMenuCandidate (P : PaperProofs.Paid.Parameters) (table : MenuTable)
    (seed : P.CalibratedMenuSeed) (history : List (VisibleEvent P.sharedInstance)) : Action P.sharedInstance :=
  if historyHalted history then .stop else
  if hstage : historyCursor history < P.certificate.stages then
    let stage : P.sharedInstance.Stage := ⟨historyCursor history, by simpa [sharedInstance] using hstage⟩
    let entry := menuEntryAt table (P.certificate.stages - stage.val)
      (P.menuEntryTools P.certificate.stages P.tools history stage)
    match historyWrite history stage with
    | none => match entry.action with
      | .finish | .abandon => .abandon
      | .test level _ => P.calibratedTestingAction level seed history stage
    | some (bit, serial) => match historyReport history stage with
      | none => .abandon
      | some (truth, reportedSerial) =>
          if serial != reportedSerial then .abandon else
          if bit == truth then .advance stage else
          match entry.action with
          | .test _ .repair => P.menuRepairAction P.certificate.stages P.tools history stage
          | _ => .abandon
  else if historyCursor history = P.certificate.stages then .stop else .abandon

original_evidence.text:
Compute $q_m$ exactly with a length-$Q$ rational random-walk table,
absorbing at $\pm(m+1)$ and applying its terminal MAP/tie decision.
With probability
\begin{equation}
 \omega_m=\frac{1/2-p_m}{1/2-q_m}
 \label{eq:paid:calibration-weight}
\end{equation}
use that capped test, and otherwise guess blindly.  It has error
exactly $p_m$.  Symmetry gives the same two truth-conditional errors;
all computations use the public channel, not an unknown true bit.

Its mean charge is at most $\mathsf C_{m+1}$, because capping and blind mixing
only reduce that unrestricted mean.  Lemma~\ref{lem:paid:surrogate}'s ratio
calculation gives $\mathsf C_{m+1}\le4\mathsf C_m$ for $m\ge1$.
Ignore excess actual test details and follow the stored endpoint policy.
At every entry its conditional error probability is still exactly $p_m$,
so the complete error, correction-choice and failure law is unchanged.
Actual correction fees have exactly their old distribution, including
payments before eventual failure.  Nonnegativity therefore yields
\[
 \E C_{\rm bounded}\le4U\le8V_f^\infty(\delta).
\]

structure CoinState where

  filled : ℕ
  bitsRead : ℕ

def coinInitial : CoinState := ⟨0, 0, 0, none⟩

def coinWidth (probability : Set.Icc (0 : ℚ) 1) : ℕ := natBits probability.val.den

/-- Literal private fair-bit rejection sampler. Build an unsigned width-bit
integer; accept below the rational denominator and compare with its numerator,
otherwise restart the block. Endpoints use no bits. A rejected block consumes
its bits; there is no bounded-bit completion or rational-coin oracle. -/
def coinStep (probability : Set.Icc (0 : ℚ) 1) (tape : FairTape) (state : CoinState) : Option CoinState :=
  if state.result.isSome then none else if probability.val = 0 then
    some { state with result := some false }
  else if probability.val = 1 then some { state with result := some true }
  else if state.filled < coinWidth probability then
    let bit := if tape state.bitsRead then 1 else 0

      accumulator := 2 * state.accumulator + bit
      filled := state.filled + 1
      bitsRead := state.bitsRead + 1 }
  else if state.accumulator < probability.val.den then
    some { state with result := some (decide (state.accumulator < probability.val.num.toNat)) }
  else some { state with accumulator := 0, filled := 0 }

original_evidence.text:
\paragraph{Explicit computation and bit lengths}

One penalty solve uses $O(N(K+1)(M+1))$ rational operations and
$O(N(K+1))$ stored actions and mean-value records.  There are at most
$J_{\rm bis}+2$ solves.  The calibration uses
$O(Q(M+1)^2)$ rational updates, summing the widths of the separate
birth--death walks; it is done once.  Thus the output is compact in these
displayed numerical parameters, with no exponential history tree.

Let $L$ bound the bit length of menu probabilities, menu costs, and input
fees.  The product of their denominators has $O((M+1)L)$ bits.
Depth-$N$ policy probabilities and mean costs have denominator bit length
$O((N+1)(M+1)L)$, with multiplier bits added for penalty objectives.
Numerators additionally count value magnitudes and the bit lengths of
$N,K$.  The calibration denominator has $O(Q L_\gamma)$ bits, where
$L_\gamma$ is the channel input length.  Initial mixture probabilities
add endpoint and $\delta$ bit lengths.  Subtracting rational endpoint
risks does not introduce an exponential number of bits.

The positive difference $\zeta_f-\delta$ is at least the reciprocal of
$2^N$ times the denominator of $\delta$; hence
$\log(1/(\zeta_f-\delta))=O(N+L_\delta)$ when it is positive.
The bit length of a very small positive $f$ is counted in $b_f$.
For fixed rational $\gamma$, $t_0,M,Q,J_{\rm bis}$ and the foregoing bit
costs are polynomial in explicit $N$ and remaining input lengths.
For variable-precision $\gamma$, dependence on numerical $1/\gamma$ is
displayed; polynomial dependence on $\log(1/\gamma)$ is not asserted.
Exact rational coins can be sampled with ordinary private randomness;
they consume no native observation or correction call.

original_evidence.text:
\paragraph{Explicit computation and bit lengths}

One penalty solve uses $O(N(K+1)(M+1))$ rational operations and
$O(N(K+1))$ stored actions and mean-value records.  There are at most
$J_{\rm bis}+2$ solves.  The calibration uses
$O(Q(M+1)^2)$ rational updates, summing the widths of the separate
birth--death walks; it is done once.  Thus the output is compact in these
displayed numerical parameters, with no exponential history tree.

Let $L$ bound the bit length of menu probabilities, menu costs, and input
fees.  The product of their denominators has $O((M+1)L)$ bits.
Depth-$N$ policy probabilities and mean costs have denominator bit length
$O((N+1)(M+1)L)$, with multiplier bits added for penalty objectives.
Numerators additionally count value magnitudes and the bit lengths of
$N,K$.  The calibration denominator has $O(Q L_\gamma)$ bits, where
$L_\gamma$ is the channel input length.  Initial mixture probabilities
add endpoint and $\delta$ bit lengths.  Subtracting rational endpoint
risks does not introduce an exponential number of bits.

The positive difference $\zeta_f-\delta$ is at least the reciprocal of
$2^N$ times the denominator of $\delta$; hence
$\log(1/(\zeta_f-\delta))=O(N+L_\delta)$ when it is positive.
The bit length of a very small positive $f$ is counted in $b_f$.
For fixed rational $\gamma$, $t_0,M,Q,J_{\rm bis}$ and the foregoing bit
costs are polynomial in explicit $N$ and remaining input lengths.
For variable-precision $\gamma$, dependence on numerical $1/\gamma$ is
displayed; polynomial dependence on $\log(1/\gamma)$ is not asserted.
Exact rational coins can be sampled with ordinary private randomness;
they consume no native observation or correction call.

Let $L$ bound the bit length of menu probabilities, menu costs, and input
fees.  The product of their denominators has $O((M+1)L)$ bits.
Depth-$N$ policy probabilities and mean costs have denominator bit length
$O((N+1)(M+1)L)$, with multiplier bits added for penalty objectives.
Numerators additionally count value magnitudes and the bit lengths of
$N,K$.  The calibration denominator has $O(Q L_\gamma)$ bits, where
$L_\gamma$ is the channel input length.  Initial mixture probabilities
add endpoint and $\delta$ bit lengths.  Subtracting rational endpoint
risks does not introduce an exponential number of bits.

The positive difference $\zeta_f-\delta$ is at least the reciprocal of
$2^N$ times the denominator of $\delta$; hence
$\log(1/(\zeta_f-\delta))=O(N+L_\delta)$ when it is positive.
The bit length of a very small positive $f$ is counted in $b_f$.
For fixed rational $\gamma$, $t_0,M,Q,J_{\rm bis}$ and the foregoing bit
costs are polynomial in explicit $N$ and remaining input lengths.
For variable-precision $\gamma$, dependence on numerical $1/\gamma$ is
displayed; polynomial dependence on $\log(1/\gamma)$ is not asserted.
Exact rational coins can be sampled with ordinary private randomness;
they consume no native observation or correction call.

\subsubsection{Proof of the price separation}
\label{sec:paid:separation}

\begin{lemma}[No-correction comparison]
\label{lem:paid:no-correction}
In the cap-relaxed model,
$V_f^\infty(\delta)\le7S_\delta$ for every $f\ge0$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At every stage take the least positive odd number $t$ of reviews such that
$(1-4\gamma^2)^t\le(\delta/N)^2$, and write its majority.
The BSC Chernoff bound gives each error at most $\delta/N$; a union bound
makes the task $\delta$-safe without any correction.
Odd rounding and $-\log(1-4\gamma^2)\ge4\gamma^2$ give
\[
 t\le\frac{\log(N/\delta)}{2\gamma^2}+2.
\]
From $h=2\operatorname{arctanh}(2\gamma)$,
\[
 8\gamma^2\le\kappa\le\frac{32}{3}\gamma^2.
\]

Suppose a retained-payment contract permits all correction obligations to
remain unpaid until a final barrier.  Consider zero review quotas,
$K=N-1$, $\delta=2^{-N}$, and $N\ge6$.  Guess all bits blindly and,
with $Z\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,1/2)$, correct exactly its $Z$ errors
when $Z<N$; abandon without correction payment when $Z=N$.
This has the minimum blind risk and expected correction count
\[
 r=N/2-N\delta.
\]
All $N$ posterior MAP errors equal $1/2$, but
$r+\delta=N/2-(N-1)\delta<N(1-\delta)/2$ for $N>2$.

charge, although the policy buys none.  The successful-path correction
requirement alone therefore does not prove our current-payment usage
inequality.  An irrevocable assignment whose payment can still be
withheld on abandonment has this same financial issue.

retained payment.  It also does not invalidate the main fixed-fee

def SharedPoolSubproblemRank : Prop :=
  ∀ n k : ℕ,
    errorRank (freshInstance n k).compatibility (freshInstance n k).tools =
      if n ≤ k then ⊤ else ((k + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞)

/-- A shared-pool rank calculation over the already independent game
semantics. The available set may be empty or a proper subset of all tools. -/
theorem sharedPool_rank_replicate {Tool : Type*} [Fintype Tool] [DecidableEq Tool]
    (n : ℕ) (remaining : Finset Tool) :
    errorRank (List.replicate n (Finset.univ : Finset Tool)) remaining =
      if n ≤ remaining.card then ⊤ else ((remaining.card + 1 : ℕ) : ℕ∞) := by
  induction n generalizing remaining with
  | zero => simp only [List.replicate_zero, errorRank_terminal, Nat.zero_le, ite_true]
  | succ n ih =>
    by_cases hempty : remaining = ∅
    · subst remaining
      rw [List.replicate_succ, errorRank_no_tools]
      simp
    · have hne : remaining.Nonempty := Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty.mpr hempty
      have hcard : 0 < remaining.card := Finset.card_pos.mpr hne
      have hcardone : remaining.card - 1 + 1 = remaining.card := by omega
      have hchild (tool : Tool) (htool : tool ∈ remaining) :
          errorRank (List.replicate n (Finset.univ : Finset Tool)) (remaining.erase tool) =
            if n ≤ remaining.card - 1 then ⊤ else (remaining.card : ℕ∞) := by
        rw [ih, Finset.card_erase_of_mem htool, hcardone]
      have hbad : badChildRank (Finset.univ : Finset Tool)
          (List.replicate n Finset.univ) remaining =
          if n ≤ remaining.card - 1 then ⊤ else (remaining.card : ℕ∞) := by
        apply le_antisymm
        · apply Finset.sup_le
          intro tool htool
          exact (hchild tool (Finset.mem_inter.mp htool).2).le
        · obtain ⟨tool, htool⟩ := hne
          have hh := childRank_le_badChildRank (Finset.univ : Finset Tool)
            (List.replicate n Finset.univ) remaining (Finset.mem_inter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ tool, htool⟩)
          rwa [hchild tool htool] at hh
      rw [List.replicate_succ, errorRank_cons, ih, hbad]
      by_cases hn : n < remaining.card
      · have hsucc : n + 1 ≤ remaining.card := by omega
        have hprev : n ≤ remaining.card - 1 := by omega
        simp [hsucc, hn.le, hprev]
      · have hsucc : ¬ n + 1 ≤ remaining.card := by omega
        have hprev : ¬ n ≤ remaining.card - 1 := by omega
        by_cases hgood : n ≤ remaining.card
        · simp [hsucc, hprev, hgood, add_comm]
        · simp [hsucc, hprev, hgood, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one, add_comm]

theorem sharedPoolSubproblemRank : SharedPoolSubproblemRank := by
  intro n k
  dsimp (config := { instances := true }) only [freshInstance, Instance.tools, Instance.Tool]
  simpa only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] using
    sharedPool_rank_replicate n (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k))

      badChildRank (P.sharedInstance.eligible stage)
        (P.sharedInstance.compatibility.drop (stage.val + 1)) P.sharedInstance.tools =
        if P.tools = 0 then 0
